current_prompt.body:
EXPLAIN why a sorting algorithm cannot simultaneously satisfy the following
be comparison‑based, have O(n) worst‑case time complexity, be stable, and sort in‑place using O(1) extra space.
DISCUSS the information‑theoretic lower bound for comparison‑based sorting (Ω(n log n)).
ARGUE that satisfying the lower bound conflicts with the O(n) worst‑case time requirement.
ARGUE that achieving O(1) extra space in‑place sorting imposes constraints that, together with stability, prevent attaining O(n) worst‑case time for comparison‑based methods.
ENSURE no code is provided that claims to meet all four constraints.
DO NOT propose any algorithm that fulfills the impossible combination.
STATE the conclusion that meeting all four constraints simultaneously is impossible for comparison‑based sorting algorithms.
